bootstrap.semantic_freeze: exact two-pass root/config bootstrap completed before own-state/public-source semantics; no later control/config semantic body ingested

findings.evidence: ToolRouter.call is the shared route gate and registered ToolCallContext extraction supplies RequestContext, Parameters, RequestState and InputResponses before the handler body. A task-capable registered handler can therefore preserve router disable/route lookup and standard argument extraction while checking Tasks capability, side-effect-free MRTR/preflight, continuation validity and current policy before task materialization.
findings.scope_limit: This is an exact-source-supported seam, not an upstream patch compiled against rmcp in this run; the bundled TaskDemo does not use this router-first shape.

findings.evidence: TaskDemo.call_tool branches on slow_sum plus client Tasks capability, manually parses arguments and calls TaskManager.spawn before its ToolRouter.call fallback. Therefore ToolRouter-local disable/configuration is not mechanically inherited by the task branch.
findings.scope_limit: This is a structural policy-parity boundary, not a claim of a demonstrated exploit in the bundled demo.

findings.evidence: Generic Server service handling awaits self.call_tool first, then rejects a Task response when the client did not advertise Tasks. A custom call_tool can therefore materialize/spawn before the generic guard rejects the response. The bundled TaskDemo separately checks capability before spawn, but the framework post-handler guard itself is not a pre-materialization fence.

The bundled TaskManager uses an in-memory HashMap and fresh UUID task IDs. No stock caller-stable reserve/create-or-get primitive or default persistent backend was found in the pinned source, so lost-CreateTaskResult blind retry and server-restart recovery remain unresolved for the stock path.
findings.scope_limit: Custom ServerHandler/storage implementations may add persistence/idempotency; this finding is not generalized to all rmcp applications.

findings.evidence: Even a persistent/redrivable task executor does not prove exactly-once external effects. Effect-side stable idempotency identity or an atomic CAS/fencing boundary remains separately required when stale attempts can overlap.
